   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c70504981" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Segment Information </span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The principal business of the Company is overseeing the business of the Bank. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant assets other than its investment in the Bank. The banking operation is the Company&#x2019;s only reportable segment. The banking segment is principally engaged in the business of originating mortgage loans secured by <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-to-<em style="font: inherit;">four</em> family residences, multi-family, construction, commercial and consumer loans. These loans are funded primarily through the attraction of deposits from the general public, borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank and brokered deposits. Selected information is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> presented separately for the Company&#x2019;s reportable segment, as there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material difference between that information and the corresponding information in the consolidated financial statements.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" id="c70504982" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">General Litigation</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company and the Bank, from time to time, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be parties to ordinary routine litigation, which arises in the normal course of business, such as claims to enforce liens, and condemnation proceedings, on properties in which the Bank holds security interests, claims involving the making and servicing of real property loans, and other issues incident to the business of the Company and the Bank. After reviewing pending and threatened litigation with legal counsel, management believes that as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>the outcome of any such litigation will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial position or results of operations.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk" id="c70504984" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Concentration of Cash Holdings</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During the normal course of business, the Bank <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have excess cash on deposit at other financial institution&#x2019;s. Each institution&#x2019;s deposits are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#x201c;FDIC&#x201d;) up to <em style="font: inherit;">$250,000.</em> At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>the Bank had $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486748" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashUninsuredAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">70.9</ix:nonFraction> million in deposits above FDIC insured limits. These funds are held with <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> institutions that are each shown to be well capitalized as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020. </em>Additionally, the Bank held $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486750" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-FederalReserveBankMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestBearingDepositsInBanks" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">65.1</ix:nonFraction> million in deposits at the Federal Reserve Bank at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020.</em></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><em style="font: inherit;"></em></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>ACQUISITION </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2, 2018, </em>the Company completed the acquisition of Carthage, Missouri-based Hometown Bancshares, Inc. (&#x201c;Hometown&#x201d;) including its wholly owned bank subsidiary, Hometown Bank, National Association and Hometown Bancshares Statutory Trust I, a Delaware statutory trust. Under the terms of the Agreement and Plan of Merger, each share of Hometown common stock was exchanged for $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486752" contextRef="i_2018-04-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionSharePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">20.00</ix:nonFraction> in cash and the transaction was valued at approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486753" contextRef="d_2018-04-02_2018-04-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">4.6</ix:nonFraction> million. Hometown&#x2019;s subsidiary bank, Hometown Bank, National Association, was merged into Guaranty Bank on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 8, 2018.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Including the effects of the acquisition method accounting adjustments, the Company acquired approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486754" contextRef="i_2018-04-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-7">180.0</ix:nonFraction> million in assets, including approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486755" contextRef="i_2018-04-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="gfed:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedLoansNet" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">143.9</ix:nonFraction> million in loans (inclusive of loan discounts) and approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486756" contextRef="i_2018-04-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="gfed:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedDeposits" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">161.2</ix:nonFraction> million in deposits. Goodwill of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486757" contextRef="i_2018-04-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million was recorded as a result of the transaction. The merger strengthened the Company&#x2019;s position in Southwest Missouri and the Company believed it would be able to achieve cost savings by integrating the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> companies and combining accounting, data processing, and other administrative functions all of which gave rise to the goodwill recorded. The goodwill will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be deductible for tax purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for acquisition accounting, the loans acquired through the acquisition of Hometown were recorded at fair value; therefore, there was <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> allowance associated with Hometown&#x2019;s loans at acquisition. Management continues to evaluate the allowance needed on the acquired Hometown loans factoring in the net remaining discount of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486761" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="gfed:BusinessCombinationAcquiredReceivablesRemainingDiscount" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">550,000</ix:nonFraction> at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Gross gains of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486767" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedGain" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">552,366</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486768" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedGain" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">244,777</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486769" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedGain" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">48,931</ix:nonFraction> and gross losses of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486770" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">91,337</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486771" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">155,213</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486772" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">57,022</ix:nonFraction> resulting from sale of available-for-sale securities were realized for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018,</em> respectively.    <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company evaluates all securities quarterly to determine if any unrealized losses are deemed to be other than temporary. Certain investment securities are valued less than their historical cost. These declines are primarily the result of the rate for these investments yielding less than current market rates or declines in stock prices of equity securities. Based on evaluation of available evidence, management believes the declines in fair value for these securities are temporary. It is management&#x2019;s intent to hold the debt securities to maturity or until recovery of the unrealized loss. Should the impairment of any of these debt securities become other than temporary, the cost basis of the investment will be reduced and the resulting loss recognized in net income in the period the other-than-temporary impairment is identified, to the extent the loss is related to credit issues, and to other comprehensive income to the extent the decline on debt securities is related to other factors and the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to sell the security prior to recovery of the unrealized loss.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><em style="font: inherit;">No</em> securities were written down for other-than-temporary impairment during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Certain investments in debt securities are reported in the consolidated financial statements at an amount less than their historical cost. Total fair value of these investments at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486787" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPosition" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">30,049,473</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486788" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPosition" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">42,570,363</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, which is approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c70486789" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:PercentageofAvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesInContinuousUnrealizedLossPositionToTotalInvestmentPortfolio" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">18</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c70486790" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:PercentageofAvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesInContinuousUnrealizedLossPositionToTotalInvestmentPortfolio" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">36</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#x2019;s investment portfolio. These declines primarily resulted from changes in market interest rates.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">A loan is considered impaired, in accordance with the impairment accounting guidance (ASC-<em style="font: inherit;">310</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">35</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">16</em>), when based on current information and events, it is probable the Bank will be unable to collect all amounts due from the borrower in accordance with the contractual terms of the loan. Impaired loans include nonperforming commercial loans but also include loans modified in troubled debt restructurings where concessions have been granted to borrowers experiencing financial difficulties. These concessions could include a reduction in the interest rate on the loan, payment extensions, forgiveness of principal, forbearance or other actions intended to maximize collection.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>the Bank&#x2019;s impaired loans shown in the table above included loans that were classified as troubled debt restructurings (TDR). The restructuring of a loan is considered a TDR if both (i) the borrower is experiencing financial difficulties and (ii) the creditor has granted a concession.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In assessing whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a borrower is experiencing financial difficulties, the Bank considers information currently available regarding the financial condition of the borrower. This information includes, but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, whether (i) the debtor is currently in payment default on any of its debt; (ii) a payment default is probable in the foreseeable future without the modification; (iii) the debtor has declared or is in the process of declaring bankruptcy and (iv) the debtor&#x2019;s projected cash flow is sufficient to satisfy the contractual payments due under the original terms of the loan without a modification.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Bank considers all aspects of the modification to loan terms to determine whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a concession has been granted to the borrower. Key factors considered by the Bank include the debtor&#x2019;s ability to access funds at a market rate for debt with similar risk characteristics, the significance of the modification relative to unpaid principal balance or collateral value of the debt, and the significance of a delay in the timing of payments relative to the original contractual terms of the loan. The most common concessions granted by the Bank generally include <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more modifications to the terms of the debt, such as (i) a reduction in the interest rate for the remaining life of the debt, (ii) an extension of the maturity date at an interest rate lower than the current market rate for new debt with similar risk, (iii) a reduction of the face amount or maturity amount of the debt as stated in the original loan, (iv) a temporary period of interest-only payments, (v) a reduction in accrued interest, and (vi) an extension of amortization.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2020, </em>our regulators issued a statement titled &#x201c;Interagency Statement on Loan Modifications and Reporting for Financial institutions with Customers Affected by the Coronavirus&#x201d; that encouraged financial institutions to work prudently with borrowers who were expected to have difficulty in meeting payment obligations due to the effects of COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19.</em> Additionally, Section <em style="font: inherit;">4013</em> of the CARES Act further clarifies that qualified loan modifications are exempt by law from being classified as a TDR as defined by GAAP from <em style="font: inherit;"> March 1, 2020 </em>until <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020. </em>In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2020, </em>the Economic Aid to Hard Hit Small Businesses, Non-Profits and Ventures Act was enacted, which extended the CARES Act provisions until <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2022. </em>The Bank continues to work with impacted entities in the form of modifications, payment deferrals, extensions of repayment terms and/or other delays in payments, as necessary.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Due to the before mentioned regulatory changes, there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> troubled debt restructuring charge offs or increases to the allowance for loan losses related to TDRs during <em style="font: inherit;">2020.</em> In <em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em> there were <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70486816">no</span> debt restructuring charge offs and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486817" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_LoanRestructuringModificationAxis-TroubledDebtRestructuringsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">37,379</ix:nonFraction> in increased allowances for loan losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Impacts from COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> have increased loan payment deferrals and other loan modifications in our loan portfolio. During <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> guidance by federal banking regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) and provisions within the CARES Act noted that short-term loan modifications made in response to COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> to borrowers with a current payment status are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered troubled debt restructurings (TDRs) for reporting purposes. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><ix:nonFraction id="c70486822" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:FinancingReceivableCOVID19ModificationsNumberOfContracts" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">20</ix:nonFraction> loans with an aggregate balance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486823" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="gfed:FinancingReceivableCOVID19ModificationsAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">28.6</ix:nonFraction> million remained modified for periods from <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months. <ix:nonFraction id="c70486826" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:FinancingReceivableCovid19ModificationsResumedScheduledPaymentPercentageOfLoan" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">84</ix:nonFraction>% of loan modifications made during <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> have resumed scheduled payments with the remaining <ix:nonFraction id="c70486828" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:FinancingReceivableCovid19ModificationsProjectedToReturnToContractualPaymentTermsPercentageOfLoan" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">16</ix:nonFraction>% projected to return to their contractual payment terms with the next <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months. Additional details on the modified loans are in the following table.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">As part of the on-going monitoring of the credit quality of the Bank&#x2019;s loan portfolio, management tracks loans by an internal rating system. All loans are assigned an internal credit quality rating based on an analysis of the borrower&#x2019;s financial condition. The criteria used to assign quality ratings to extensions of credit that exhibit potential problems or well-defined weaknesses are primarily based upon the degree of risk and the likelihood of orderly repayment, and their effect on the Bank&#x2019;s safety and soundness. The following are the internally assigned ratings:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Pass- This rating represents loans that have strong asset quality and liquidity along with a multi-year track record of profitability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Special mention- This rating represents loans that are currently protected but are potentially weak. The credit risk <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be relatively minor, yet constitute an increased risk in light of the circumstances surrounding a specific loan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Substandard- This rating represents loans that show signs of continuing negative financial trends and unprofitability and therefore, is inadequately protected by the current sound worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Doubtful- This rating represents loans that have all the weaknesses of substandard classified loans with the additional characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions and values, highly questionable and improbable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Risk characteristics applicable to each segment of the loan portfolio are described as follows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Real estate-Residential <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> family: The residential <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> family real estate loans are generally secured by owner-occupied <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> family residences. Repayment of these loans is primarily dependent on the personal income and credit rating of the borrowers. Credit risk in these loans can be impacted by economic conditions within the Bank&#x2019;s market areas that might impact either property values or a borrower&#x2019;s personal income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Risk is mitigated by the fact that the loans are of smaller individual amounts and spread over a large number of borrowers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Real estate-Construction: Construction and land development real estate loans are usually based upon estimates of costs and estimated value of the completed project and include independent appraisal reviews and a financial analysis of the developers and property owners. Sources of repayment of these loans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include permanent loans, sales of developed property or an interim loan commitment from the Bank until permanent financing is obtained. These loans are considered to be higher risk than other real estate loans due to their ultimate repayment being sensitive to interest rate changes, general economic conditions and the availability of long-term financing. Credit risk in these loans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be impacted by the creditworthiness of a borrower, property values and the local economies in the Bank&#x2019;s market areas.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Real estate-Commercial: Commercial real estate loans typically involve larger principal amounts, and repayment of these loans is generally dependent on the successful operations of the property securing the loan or the business conducted on the property securing the loan. These loans are viewed primarily as cash flow loans and secondarily as loans secured by real estate. Credit risk in these loans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be impacted by the creditworthiness of a borrower, property values and the local economies in the Bank&#x2019;s market areas.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Commercial: The commercial portfolio includes loans to commercial customers for use in financing working capital needs, equipment purchases and expansions. The loans in this category are repaid primarily from the cash flow of a borrower&#x2019;s principal business operation. Credit risk in these loans is driven by creditworthiness of a borrower and the economic conditions that impact the cash flow stability from business operations. Included in this category as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>are $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486840" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_LoansInsuredOrGuaranteedByGovernmentAuthoritiesAxis-SBACaresActPaycheckProtectionProgramMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableNetReportedAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">37.3</ix:nonFraction> million in Small Business Administration PPP loans originated during the year with the majority of the loans having an original duration of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> years or less.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Consumer: The consumer loan portfolio consists of various term and line of credit loans such as automobile loans and loans for other personal purposes. Repayment for these types of loans will come from a borrower&#x2019;s income sources that are typically independent of the loan purpose. Credit risk is driven by consumer economic factors (such as unemployment and general economic conditions in the Bank&#x2019;s market area) and the creditworthiness of a borrower.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The following table provides information about the credit quality of the loan portfolio using the Bank&#x2019;s internal rating system as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019:</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:AccountingForCertainLoansAndDebtSecuritiesAcquiredInTransferDisclosureTextBlock" id="c1774219" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">5:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>ACCOUNTING FOR CERTAIN LOANS ACQUIRED</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company acquired loans during the quarter ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2018 </em>as part of the acquisition of Hometown. At acquisition, certain acquired loans evidenced deterioration of credit quality since origination and it was probable, at acquisition, that all contractually required payments would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be collected.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Loans purchased with the evidence of credit deterioration since origination and for which it is probable that all contractually required payments will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be collected are considered to be credit impaired. Evidence of credit quality deterioration as of the purchase date <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include information such as past-due and nonaccrual status, borrower credit scores or recent loan to value percentages. Purchased credit impaired loans are accounted for under the accounting guidance for loans and debt securities acquired with deteriorated credit quality (ASC <em style="font: inherit;">310</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">30</em>) and initially measured at fair value, which includes estimated future credit losses expected to be incurred over the life of the loan. Accordingly, an allowance for credit losses related to these loans is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> carried over and recorded at the acquisition date. Management estimated the cash flows expected to be collected at acquisition using our internal risk models, which incorporate the estimate of current key assumptions, such as default rates, severity and prepayment speeds. Loan accretion income recognized during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> were $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486863" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="gfed:CertainLoansAcquiredInTransferNotAccountedForAsDebtSecuritiesFullPayoffOfCertainPurchasedCreditImpairedLoans" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4">0.41</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486864" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="gfed:CertainLoansAcquiredInTransferNotAccountedForAsDebtSecuritiesFullPayoffOfCertainPurchasedCreditImpairedLoans" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4">1.49</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The carrying amount of remaining purchased credit impaired loans are included in the balance sheet amounts of loans receivable at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019.</em> The amount of these loans is shown below:</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486871" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million of goodwill as a result of its <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> Hometown acquisition and the goodwill is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deductible for tax purposes. Goodwill is assessed annually, or more often if warranted, for impairment. If the implied fair value of goodwill is lower than its carrying amount, goodwill impairment is indicated, and goodwill is written down to its implied value. Goodwill impairment was neither indicated nor recorded during <em style="font: inherit;">2020.</em> Subsequent increases in goodwill value are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized in the financial statements. Goodwill totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486876" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em> respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">8:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>LEASES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">As discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">19,</em> on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2019, </em>the Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02,</em> &#x201c;Leases&#x201d;. The Company recorded initial balances during the quarter ending <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2019 </em>for operating Right of Use (&#x201c;ROU&#x201d;) assets and liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486889" contextRef="i_2019-01-01" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">9,655,304</ix:nonFraction>. Additionally, the Company recorded initial balances for financing ROU assets and liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486890" contextRef="i_2019-01-01" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinanceLeaseLiability" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">481,830</ix:nonFraction>. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>operating lease liability balances were $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486891" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">8,560,892</ix:nonFraction> and financing lease liability amounts were $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486892" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinanceLeaseLiability" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">510,526</ix:nonFraction>. We maintain operating leases on land and buildings for certain branch facilities and our headquarters. Financing leases are primarily for equipment used at banking facilities. Most leases include options to renew, with renewal terms extending between <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70486893">one</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70486894">twenty</span> years. The exercise of renewal options is based on judgement of management as to whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the renewal option is reasonably certain to be exercised. Factors in determining whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the renewal option is reasonably certain to be exercised include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the value of the leasehold improvements, the value of the renewal rate compared to market rates and the presence of factors that would cause significant economic penalty to the Company if the option is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exercised.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Expenses for finance leases are included in other interest expense and occupancy expense line items, whereas, operating leases are expensed entirely in the occupancy expense line item. Leases with a term of less than <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded on the balance sheet and are expensed on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Discount rates used for the purpose of valuing the leases were based on rates available to the Company on fixed rate borrowings for similar lease terms.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">10:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>INVESTMENTS IN AFFORDABLE HOUSING PARTNERSHIPS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has purchased investments in limited partnerships that were formed to operate low-income housing apartment complexes and single-family housing units throughout Missouri. The investments are accounted for under the proportional amortization method if certain conditions are met. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the ability to exert significant influence over the partnerships. For a minimum <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70486909">fifteen</span>-year compliance period, each partnership must adhere to affordable housing regulatory requirements in order to maintain the utilization of the tax credits.    <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The FHLB requires the Bank to maintain collateral in relation to outstanding balances of advances. For collateral purposes, the FHLB values mortgage loans free of other pledges, liens and encumbrances at <ix:nonFraction id="c70486941" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_FairValueByAssetClassAxis-MortgageLoansFreeofOtherPledgesLiensandEncumbrancesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:FederalHomeLoanBankPercentageOfFairValueOfCollateral" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="1">80</ix:nonFraction>% of their fair value, and investment securities free of other pledges, liens and encumbrances at <ix:nonFraction id="c70486942" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_FairValueByAssetClassAxis-InvestmentSecuritiesFreeofOtherPledgesLiensandEncumbrancesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:FederalHomeLoanBankPercentageOfFairValueOfCollateral" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">95</ix:nonFraction>% of their fair value. Based on existing collateral as well as the FHLB&#x2019;s limitation of advances to <ix:nonFraction id="c70486943" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="gfed:FederalHomeLoanBankPercentageOfFairValueOfCollateral" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">45</ix:nonFraction>% of assets, the Bank has the ability to borrow an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486944" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-FederalHomeLoanBankMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">162.4</ix:nonFraction> million from the FHLB, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Federal Reserve Bank Borrowings</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2008,</em> the Bank established a borrowing line with the Federal Reserve Bank. The Bank has the ability to borrow $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486946" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-FederalReserveBankBorrowingsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">37.2</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020. </em>The Federal Reserve Bank requires the Bank to maintain collateral in relation to borrowings outstanding. The Bank had <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70486947"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70538306">no</span></span> borrowings outstanding on this line as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note Payable to Bank</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019, </em>the Company had an established note payable of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486949" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfLongTermDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">11.2</ix:nonFraction> million with another financial institution. The note was fully drawn as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019 </em>with the original purpose to provide additional capital for funding Bank asset growth and to redeem Hometown Bancshares subordinated debentures discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> The note carried a variable interest rate tied to <em style="font: inherit;">30</em>-day LIBOR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c70486952" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember_VariableRateAxis-LondonInterbankOfferedRateLIBORMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-4" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="3">250</ix:nonFraction> basis points (<ix:nonFraction id="c70486953" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateEffectivePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">4.24</ix:nonFraction>% at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019). </em>In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2020, </em>proceeds from a subordinated debt offering, discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">14,</em> were used to completely pay off the note payable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Line of Credit to Bank</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em> The Company established a $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486956" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LineOfCreditMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">3.0</ix:nonFraction> million revolving line of credit with another financial institution. The note carries a variable interest rate tied to <em style="font: inherit;">30</em>-day LIBOR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c70486958" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LineOfCreditMember_VariableRateAxis-LondonInterbankOfferedRateLIBORMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-4" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="3">250</ix:nonFraction> basis points with a floor of <ix:nonFraction id="c70486959" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LineOfCreditMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-4" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">400</ix:nonFraction> basis points and matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 28, 2021. </em><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70486960"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70538309">No</span></span> amounts were borrowed on this line as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>or <em style="font: inherit;" class="GFJY4-DIN-com-rdg-thunderdome-client-resources-CssResource-html-element-highlighted">2019.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">13:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>SUBORDINATED DEBENTURES ISSUED TO CAPITAL TRUSTS</b></p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2005,</em> the Company formed <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> wholly owned grantor trust subsidiaries, Guaranty Statutory Trust I and Guaranty Statutory Trust II, to issue preferred securities representing undivided beneficial interests in the assets of the trusts and to invest the gross proceeds of the preferred securities in notes of the Company.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As part of the <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2, 2018 </em>acquisition of Hometown Bancshares, Inc., and pursuant to a Second Supplemental Indenture by and among the Company, Hometown and Wilmington Trust Company, as Trustee, the Company assumed Hometown&#x2019;s rights, duties and obligations under the original Indenture of a wholly owned subsidiary, Hometown Bancshares Capital Trust I, a Delaware statutory trust formed on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 29, 2002. </em>This Trust was formed for the purposes of issuing $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486975" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_SubordinatedBorrowingAxis-HometownBancsharesCapitalTrustIMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">6.0</ix:nonFraction> million of Trust Preferred Securities.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">14:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>SUBORDINATED NOTES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 29, 2020, </em>the Company completed a private offering of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486986" contextRef="i_2020-07-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesNetMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-7">20.0</ix:nonFraction> million aggregate principal amount of <ix:nonFraction id="c70486987" contextRef="i_2020-07-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesNetMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">5.25</ix:nonFraction>% fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes due <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em> (the &#x201c;Notes&#x201d;). The Notes were issued by the Company to the purchasers at a price equal to <em style="font: inherit;">100%</em> of their face amount. Costs related to the issuance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70486990" contextRef="d_2020-07-29_2020-07-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesNetMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfDebtIssuanceCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">454,445</ix:nonFraction> reduced the proceeds received by the Company and will be amortized over the life of the notes. The Notes are intended to qualify as Tier <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> capital for regulatory purposes. The Notes have a stated maturity of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2030, </em>are redeemable by the Company at its option, in whole or in part, on or after <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>and at any time upon the occurrences of certain events. Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>redeem the Notes, in whole but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> in part, only under certain limited circumstances set forth in the Note. On or after <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>redeem the Notes, in whole or in part, at its option, on any interest payment date. Any redemption by the Company would be at a redemption price equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c70486993" contextRef="d_2020-07-29_2020-07-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesNetMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the principal amount of the Notes being redeemed, together with any accrued and unpaid interest on the Notes being redeemed to but excluding the date of redemption. The Notes are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to redemption at the option of the holder. The Notes will bear interest at a fixed rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c70486995" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesNetMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_StatementScenarioAxis-ScenarioForecastMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">5.25</ix:nonFraction>% per year until <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025 </em>or earlier redemption date. From <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2025 </em>to, but excluding the maturity date or earlier redemption date, the interest rate will reset quarterly at a variable rate equal to the then current <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-month term SOFR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c70486997" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2025-10-01_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesNetMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_StatementScenarioAxis-ScenarioForecastMember_VariableRateAxis-SecuredOvernightFinancingRateSofrOvernightIndexSwapRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-4" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">519</ix:nonFraction> basis points. Principal and interest on the Notes are subject to acceleration only in limited circumstances. The Notes are unsecured, subordinated obligations of the Company, are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obligations of, and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> guaranteed by, any subsidiary of the Company, and rank junior in right of payment to the Company&#x2019;s current and future senior indebtedness.</p>

This amount represents an allocation of income to bad debt deductions for tax purposes only. The unrecorded deferred income tax liability on the above amount was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70487005" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_ValuationAllowanceByDeferredTaxAssetAxis-AllocationofIncometoBadDebtDeductionsforTaxPurposesOnlyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">1,218,000</ix:nonFraction> as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020.</em></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c1774246" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">16:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>DISCLOSURES ABOUT FAIR VALUE OF ASSETS AND LIABILITIES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurements</i>, defines fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820</em> also specifies a fair value hierarchy which requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value. The standard describes <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels of inputs that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be used to measure fair value:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em></b>:&#xa0; Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em></b>: Observable inputs other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em></b>: Unobservable inputs supported by little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity and are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The following is a description of the inputs and valuation methodologies used for assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis and recognized in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets, as well as the general classification of such assets pursuant to the valuation hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Available-for-sale securities:</i> Where quoted market prices are available in an active market, securities are classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the valuation hierarchy. Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> securities include equity securities. If quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, then fair values are estimated by using pricing models, quoted prices of securities with similar characteristics or discounted cash flows. Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities include U.S. government agencies, municipals, U.S. corporate and government sponsored and other mortgage-backed securities. The Company has <ix:nonFraction id="c70487023" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel3Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecurities" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Derivative financial instruments (Cash flow hedges):</i> The Company&#x2019;s open derivative positions are interest rate swap agreements. Those classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> open derivative positions are valued using externally developed pricing models based on observable market inputs provided by a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party and validated by management. The Company has considered counterparty credit risk in the valuation of its interest rate swap assets.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The following is a description of the valuation methodologies used for assets measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis and recognized in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets, as well as the general classification of such assets pursuant to the valuation hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Foreclosed Assets Held for Sale: </i>Fair value is estimated using recent appraisals, comparable sales and other estimates of value obtained principally from independent sources, adjusted for selling costs. Foreclosed assets held for sale are classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> of the valuation hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Impaired loans (Collateral Dependent):</i> Loans for which it is probable that the Company will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collect all principal and interest due according to contractual terms are measured for impairment. Allowable methods for determining the amount of impairment include estimating fair value using the fair value of the collateral for collateral dependent loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">If the impaired loan is identified as collateral dependent, then the fair value method of measuring the amount of impairment is utilized. This method requires obtaining a current independent appraisal of the collateral and applying a discount factor to the value. Impaired loans that are collateral dependent are classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> of the fair value hierarchy when impairment is determined using the fair value method.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The following methods were used to estimate the fair value of all other financial instruments recognized in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets at amounts other than fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Cash and cash equivalents, interest-bearing deposits and Federal Home Loan Bank stock</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The carrying amounts reported in the consolidated balance sheets approximate those assets' fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Held-to-maturity securities</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Fair value is based on quoted market prices, if available. If a quoted market price is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair value is estimated using quoted market prices for similar securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Loans</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The fair value of loans is estimated on an exit price basis incorporating contractual cash flow, prepayment discount spreads, credit loss and liquidity premiums.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Deposits</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Deposits include demand deposits, savings accounts, NOW accounts and certain money market deposits. The carrying amount approximates fair value. The fair value of fixed-maturity certificates of deposit is estimated by discounting the future cash flows using rates currently offered for deposits of similar remaining maturities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Federal Home Loan Bank advances </span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The fair value of advances is estimated by using rates on debt with similar terms and remaining maturities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Subordinated debentures and Note Payable to Bank</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">For these variable rate instruments, the carrying amount is a reasonable estimate of fair value. There is currently a limited market for similar debt instruments and the Company has the option to call the subordinated debentures at an amount close to its par value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Subordinated notes</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">For these fixed rate instruments, the fair value is calculated over the remaining term of the notes compared to similar duration products. There is currently a limited market for similar debt instruments and the Company has the option to call the subordinated notes at par in <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Interest payable</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The carrying amount approximates fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Commitments to originate loans, letters of credit and lines of credit</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The fair value of commitments to originate loans is estimated using the fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the present credit worthiness of the counterparties. For fixed-rate loan commitments, fair value also considers the difference between current levels of interest rates and the committed rates. The fair value of letters of credit and lines of credit is based on fees currently charged for similar agreements or on the estimated cost to terminate them or otherwise settle the obligations with the counterparties at the reporting date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">17:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>SIGNIFICANT ESTIMATES AND CONCENTRATIONS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America require disclosure of certain significant estimates and current vulnerabilities due to certain concentrations. Estimates related to the allowance for loan losses are reflected in the footnote regarding loans. Current vulnerabilities due to certain concentrations of credit risk are discussed in the footnote regarding loans.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">18:</em></b>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;<b>EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Equity Plans</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 27, 2015, </em>the Company&#x2019;s stockholders voted to approve the Guaranty Federal Bancshares, Inc. <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Equity Plan (<em style="font: inherit;">the&#x201d;2015</em> Plan&#x201d;). The Plan provides for the grant of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c70487044" contextRef="i_2015-05-27_PlanNameAxis-EquityPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">250,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock under equity awards including stock options, stock awards, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights, performance units, or other equity-based awards payable in cash or stock to key employees and directors of the Company and the Bank. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>restricted stock for <ix:nonFraction id="c70487045" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-EquityPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="gfed:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsAggregateGrants" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">90,016</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock and <ix:nonFraction id="c70487046" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceSharesMember_PlanNameAxis-EquityPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="gfed:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsAggregateGrants" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">108,898</ix:nonFraction> of performance stock units has been granted under the Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 26, 2010, </em>the Company&#x2019;s stockholders voted to approve the Guaranty Federal Bancshares, Inc. <em style="font: inherit;">2010</em> Equity Plan (<em style="font: inherit;">the&#x201d;2010</em> Plan&#x201d;). The Plan provides for the grant of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c70487049" contextRef="i_2010-05-26_PlanNameAxis-EquityPlan2010Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">200,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock under equity awards including stock options, stock awards, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights, performance units, or other equity-based awards payable in cash or stock to key employees and directors of the Company and the Bank. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>non-incentive stock options for <ix:nonFraction id="c70487050" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember_PlanNameAxis-EquityPlan2010Member" unitRef="Share" name="gfed:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsAggregateGrants" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">25,000</ix:nonFraction> shares and restricted stock for <ix:nonFraction id="c70487051" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-EquityPlan2010Member" unitRef="Share" name="gfed:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsAggregateGrants" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">139,330</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock have been granted under the Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In addition, the Company established <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> stock option plans for the benefit of certain directors, officers and employees of the Company and its subsidiary. A committee of the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors administers the plans. The stock options under these plans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be either incentive stock options or nonqualified stock options. Incentive stock options can be granted only to participants who are employees of the Company or its subsidiary. The option price must <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be less than the market value of the Company stock on the date of grant. All options expire <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> later than <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70487055">ten</span> years from the date of grant. The options vest at the rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c70487056" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_VestingAxis-AnnualVestingRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="1">20</ix:nonFraction>% per year over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70487057">five</span>-year period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
